answer.summary: The research question cannot be empirically evaluated due to absence of explicitly reported, time-bound retention metrics in Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1, necessitating a bounded revision to anchor the inquiry solely in verifiable numerical data before further
answer.content: After two independent reviews confirm the lack of numerically specified time-based retention or stability metrics for memory persistence in tokenized agents under known perturbations, the current research question remains untestable. The evidence shows no explicit duration thresholds or temporal decay rates reported in the primary source. A bounded revision is required to restrict the inquiry to only those metrics directly and numerically stated in Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1 before any further analysis can proceed. Without such anchoring, the research is not empirically grounded or falsifiable as required by the objective to test superiority through verifiable data alone.

answer.nextTask: handoff to analyst to formulate a revised research question on the minimum duration of periodic input required for observable memory persistence in a tokenized agent under known perturbations, anchored solely to explicitly reported time-based retention or stability metrics from Kumar et al., 2024, Section 4.1
answer.lesson: All memory research must be strictly grounded in explicitly reported, numerically specified retention metrics from primary sources before any empirical evaluation can occur; without such verifiable data, the research remains untestable and must be revised prior to further analysis or implementation.
